GENERAL SCIENCE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #14
====

GRADE: Grade 12
SUBJECT: GENERAL SCIENCE
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   B. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   C. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   D. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

2. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   B. Water always increases oxygen
   C. Water removes heat too quickly
   D. Petrol fires have no fuel

3. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 37 °C
   B. 0 °C
   C. 50 °C
   D. 100 °C

4. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Evolution and Biodiversity? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Evolution and Biodiversity.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Evolution and Biodiversity.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Evolution and Biodiversity.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Evolution and Biodiversity.

5. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   B. Any white crystal used in cooking
   C. A mixture of two liquids
   D. Any substance that conducts electricity

6. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Only carbon dioxide
   B. Nitrogen gas only
   C. Glucose and oxygen
   D. Only water vapour

7. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Paper burning to ash
   B. Milk souring
   C. Ice melting to water
   D. Iron rusting

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Alkanols, Alkanoic Acids and Esters.? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Alkanols, Alkanoic Acids and Esters..
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Alkanols, Alkanoic Acids and Esters..
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Alkanols, Alkanoic Acids and Esters..
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Alkanols, Alkanoic Acids and Esters..

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying The Ecosystems? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about The Ecosystems.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to The Ecosystems.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on The Ecosystems.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for The Ecosystems.

10. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. A chemical reaction forming ash
   B. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   C. Movement of water only across a membrane
   D. Heating until a solid melts

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Electrostatics? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Electrostatics.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Electrostatics.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Electrostatics.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Electrostatics.

12. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. joule (J)
   B. pascal (Pa)
   C. watt (W)
   D. newton (N)

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Alkanols, Alkanoic Acids and Esters. and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Detergents ● Soapy and soapless detergents ● Preparations of detergents ● Mode o and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Polymers and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Electrolysis and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. D — Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

2. A — Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

3. D — 100 °C

4. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Evolution and Biodiversity.

5. A — A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

6. C — Glucose and oxygen

7. C — Ice melting to water

8. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Alkanols, Alkanoic Acids and Esters..

9. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for The Ecosystems.

10. B — Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

11. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Electrostatics.

12. D — newton (N)

Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Alkanols, Alkanoic Acids and Esters.; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
